hero.name: Tarik Cavalcanti
hero.subtitle: Computer Science & Mathematical Physics Graduate • Master’s Student
hero.summary: Master’s student seeking part-time software engineering work. I enjoy building practical software systems, from web applications and infrastructure to algorithmic optimization. My experience spans full-stack development, monitoring and tooling for research infrastructure, and algorithm engineering in C++.

items.title: Teddybären Krankenhaus
items.subtitle: Full-stack web application for generating synthetic teddy-bear X-ray images using state-of-the-art machine learning models
bullets: Built an end-to-end workflow for image capture with a custom fake X-ray machine, generation task queuing, and long-term file storage.
Developed the application stack with FastAPI, SvelteKit, ComfyUI, nginx, Docker, and Seafile.
Documented, tested, and containerized the system, and set up a robust CI/CD pipeline.
Collaborated in a student team to deliver a production-deployed application used in real operations.

items.title: Weighted Connectivity Augmentation
items.subtitle: Algorithm engineering and optimization in C++
bullets: Improved on state-of-the-art approaches for the Weighted Connectivity Augmentation problem using a reduction to the Set Cover problem.
Implemented and benchmarked reduction strategies to improve performance.
Focused on practical implementation, leveraging more efficient memory access patterns and parallelization compared with existing implementations.
Derived a solution-quality bound for an existing algorithm.

items.title: Web Novel Scraping
items.subtitle: Web application for scraping, generating, and delivering EPUB files
bullets: Built a Flask- and MongoDB-based web application to scrape web novels from multiple websites and compile them into EPUB format.
Designed the application so generated files could be sent directly to e-readers.

items.title: Student Research Assistant (HiWi)
items.subtitle: Heidelberg University — Cluster Monitoring / Infrastructure Support
bullets: Helped monitor computing-cluster environments using humidity and temperature sensors placed around and inside server racks.
Collected sensor readings with Raspberry Pis; managed sensors through a Django web application; stored data in TSDBs; visualized metrics and alerts in Grafana; and handled deployment with Ansible.
Developed and maintained multiple codebases supporting cluster-monitoring infrastructure.
